title: Symbol
description: One term of the symbols class (decision D63): a symbol of the pool as itself, read as its word. One line of data/vocabulary/symbols.jsonl. The search admits it only when the class is on, and every anagram carries the class of each such term; words alone is the default everywhere. Every term is public, carries what it reads as, a meaning a reader can read and a public trace; the operator admits it by merging the pull request that adds it, and the rebuilt classes artifact is committed with [dict].

term.description: One symbol of the pool, the six that stand wherever they are in a text. `!` and `?` are characters of the pool inside a word only and read as nothing.

reads_as.description: What the term stands for when it is read: the word or words it reads as (`and` for `&`, `you` for `u`, `bait` for `b8`, `I don't know` for `idk`). Lowercase, except the word I, which is a word of English and is written as one; a reader sees it in the word panel beside the gloss.

gloss.description: What the term means, in one sentence. A reader sees this in the word panel, so PRODUCT.md's rule applies: a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end.

trace.description: Where the term is attested, always public: its Wiktionary entry, or another page anyone can open.

proposed_by.description: Who proposed it. A model or the pipeline may propose; only a merge admits.

tone.description: `crude` when the term or what it reads as is an expletive or a slur. A crude term's class is off by default, and the standing rules on anagrams of living people apply to it.

also.description: The other classes this term is listed in, when it is meant to be in more than one; the build gives it every class's bit. Without this, a term in two files is a mistake vocab:check reports.

note.description: Anything else worth recording about the admission.
